partner_results_applied.scope: Interval domination iff L-infinity density; continuity separated by Steklov regularity.
Admissible marginal-density class is the L1-closed convex hull of measure-one indicators; product laws are TV limits of finite mixtures; finite-fragment localization.

new_results: QFORM-LINFINITY-EXTREME-TRANSFER-v1: the extended output density functional M(mu)=sup_I mu(I)/|I| is convex and TV-lower-semicontinuous, so its exact supremum over all admissible measurable product densities equals its supremum over product-indicator laws, and via the consumed localization over bounded finite unions of intervals of total measure one.

QFORM-CONTINUITY-MODULUS-EXTREME-TRANSFER-v1: a common output continuity modulus plus common L-infinity bound on the extreme product-indicator class transfers to every admissible product density by finite mixtures, TV pushforward and Arzela-Ascoli.
Continuity of each extreme output plus a common L-infinity bound alone does not transfer under TV limits; mollified unit-interval densities give the abstract obstruction.
first_unresolved_implication: Dimension-free interval small-ball bound uniformly over target-admissible A and products of bounded finite unions of intervals E_i with |E_i|=1, with arbitrary fragmentation complexity and separation.
continuity_unresolved_implication: Obtain a common Steklov/equicontinuity modulus on the extreme finite-fragment class; essential boundedness alone cannot supply it.
next_step: Apply a completed geometry/small-ball result to the finite-fragment extreme class; separately derive a common output modulus from the same shell estimate if possible.
